summary: Sustained 5xx wave: API gateway ephemeral socket throttle leading to upstream runtime GPU watchdog restarts during customer burst
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightWrite reported a sudden sustained increase in 5xx responses between 18:35-19:40 PDT on 2026-03-13. Errors correlate with a large tenant burst (long-lived streaming sessions) and a concurrent increase in ephemeral socket churn at the API gateway. Upstream serving-runtime instances experienced GPU watchdog restarts and OOM-like behavior during the window.

Impact:
- BrightWrite (dedicated) observed ~40% of their requests returning 5xx intermittently; streaming sessions were frequently disconnected.
- Error spike affected their production us-west region only.

Environment:
- prod-us-west, dedicated cluster pool RB-ded-42
- Affected model routes: redwood-instruct-13b and llama3-70b-mixed pinned for the customer

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer performed a scheduled internal campaign that opened ~1.8x baseline concurrent streaming sessions starting at ~18:30 PDT.
2) API gateway ephemeral connection count (socket ephemeral port usage) increased and hit threshold on some edge nodes.
3) API gateway began returning 502/503 for new streams and started TCP resets for existing keepalives.
4) Serving-runtime backends received bursts of partial connections leading to heavy KV cache thrash and increased GPU memory volatility.
5) GPU watchdog restarts observed on several runtime pods; some restarted multiple times causing transient 5xx floor.

Observed logs/metrics (high level):
- apigw.edge.sockets.ephemeral_in_use spike to 98% on 3 nodes (normal <= 45%)
- apigw.errors.5xx increased from baseline 0.5% -> 22% (customer routes)
- runtime.gpu.watchdog_restarts: 6 events in 30m across 4 pods
- runtime.kvcache.evictions spike and prefetch queue length growth

Expected behavior:
- API gateway should gracefully queue/route without triggering connection resets; runtime should not enter watchdog restart loops under transient socket pressure.

Attachments:
- selected apigw and runtime logs (attached to ticket)
- Cloud metrics graphs (links in comments)
comments: 2026-03-13 19:02 - Support (Aisha): Initial triage performed. Collected logs and elevated to SRE. Informed customer we're investigating and requested exact timeframe and any recent config changes.

2026-03-13 19:18 - SRE (Diego): Noted socket_ephemeral_in_use spike on edge nodes edge-17/19/23. Correlated with increased long-lived streaming sessions from BrightWrite tenant. Opening infra-side investigation into accept queue sizing and keepalive behavior.
2026-03-13 19:45 - Customer (BrightWrite - Ops): Confirmed they kicked off a heavy streaming-promotional job at 18:28 PDT and saw disconnects. Asked for ETA/mitigation.

2026-03-13 20:05 - SRE (Diego): Temporarily increased per-node ephemeral port window on impacted edge nodes and applied connection drain smoothing for BrightWrite route. Observed drop in 5xx rate to ~3% within 6 minutes. Not a permanent fix.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Support (Aisha): Follow-up to customer with interim mitigation and next steps (runtime config change + infra patch scheduled). Customer satisfied with workaround but requested full root cause and timeline for permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Edge analysis: accept queue and ephemeral port exhaustion on a subset of edge nodes. Edge software did not gracefully throttle long-lived streaming accept rate; new connections triggered resets when ephemeral pool depleted.

Runtime analysis: sudden surge of half-open/short-lived connections increased memory fragmentation in serving-runtime and generated KV cache thrash; combined with large batch of streaming prefix tokens caused GPU memory pressure and watchdog restarts.

Hypothesis: combination of aggressive customer streaming concurrency + apigw accept/keepalive policy produced connection churn that amplified to runtime, causing GPU watchdog restarts (not a model bug).

Related historical tickets: SUP-214890 (stale keepalive proxy reuse), SUP-472901 (connection thrashing causing bridge 502s) — behavior similar but root cause here more focused on ephemeral socket exhaustion at edge layer.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation (completed 2026-03-13 19:55): increased ephemeral port allocation and smoothing, applied temporary route-level throttle for BrightWrite to limit concurrent streaming sessions. Result: 5xx rate reduced to ~2-4% for customer traffic.

Planned fix (scheduled): update API gateway to backpressure new long-lived streaming accepts earlier and add adaptive keepalive reclamation (patch PR https://github.com/redwood-infra/agent/pull/2345). Update serving-runtime to harden KV cache eviction under high connection churn (PR https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/987).
Customer follow-up: engineering SLOs and suggested client-side exponential backoff for streaming reconnects. Support scheduled a postmortem meeting with BrightWrite for 2026-03-16.

Post-incident tasks:
- Infra: edge accept queue autosizing + tests (owner: Edge team)
- Runtime: improve watchdog telemetry and avoid restart loops under transient memory pressure (owner: Serving Runtime team)
- Support: update runbook and add proactive alert for apigw.ephemeral_in_use > 80% (owner: Support)
